c.tagline: Ancient walls, Caspian shores, and a flame-lit skyline.

taxi.fareNote: Official Baku Taxi cabs are metered and red; agree fare upfront or use Bolt/Uber for transparent pricing, especially from the airport.

emergency.note: General emergency line 112 also connects to police, fire, and ambulance services.

avoid.reason: Safe; do not travel to Nagorno-Karabakh or front-line border areas

hood_desc: The UNESCO-listed walled Old City (Icherisheher) with cobblestone lanes, the Maiden Tower and Shirvanshahs' Palace; ideal for first-time visitors who want history and atmosphere within walking distance of everything.
Baku's lively pedestrian core around Fountains Square and Nizami Street, packed with cafes, shopping and nightlife; suits visitors who want a central base near restaurants and metro access.
The palm-lined Caspian seafront Boulevard beneath the Flame Towers in Sabayil, home to upscale hotels, parks and Crystal Hall; best for travelers wanting sea views and easy access to landmark sights.
A buzzing entertainment and dining district packed with restaurants, bars and clubs; suited to visitors who want to be close to Baku's nightlife scene.
A residential, mostly local neighborhood away from the tourist core with everyday markets, cheaper stays and easy metro links; good for budget travelers wanting an authentic, non-touristy base.

water.note: Despite treatment upgrades, most residents and all visitors are advised to use bottled or filtered water.

transit.pay: Visitors buy a rechargeable BakuKart smart card (small refundable deposit) at metro stations or kiosks, which works across metro, bus, funicular and Aeroexpress airport bus. Cards can be topped up with cash or card at station machines and validated by tapping on entry.
transit.hours: Metro operates roughly 6:00-24:00; BakuBus network runs similar hours with some 24-hour routes like the airport H1 line.
transit.note: Metro has 3 lines (Red, Green, Purple) with about 27 stations; extensive city bus network covers areas metro doesn't reach.

train: Baku Railway Station (domestic and international routes including Tbilisi and the Baku-Tbilisi-Kars line)
bus: Intercity buses from Baku International Bus Terminal
ferry: Baku International Sea Trade Port (Caspian Sea ferries to Aktau, Kazakhstan and Turkmenbashi, Turkmenistan)

transit.m: Aeroexpress bus to 28 May metro station (~30 min, every 20-60 min, 06:00-23:15)
BakuBus H1 24-hour line to city center

tip.r: Not obligatory; rounding up or leaving 5-10% at restaurants is appreciated, especially where service isn't included.
